summary: Polymorphism means one method call, like student.report(), runs the version that belongs to the object's actual class. You can loop over mixed objects and treat them the same way.
notes: HonorsStudent has no constructor, so JavaScript uses Student's constructor for it automatically.
The for...of loop never checks the type. JavaScript looks up report() on each object when the line runs.
toFixed(1) keeps one decimal place, so 81 prints as 81.0.
pitfall: Calling a method the object does not have causes TypeError: roster[0].weightedAverage is not a function, and only when that line runs.
contrast: JavaScript works like Python here: there are no declared types, so any object with a report() method can go in the loop and no cast is needed. Java checks the declared type at compile time.
